issue.title: PDF 2.0 Application Note for Associated Files is out of date
issue.body:
The "[PDF 2.0 Application Note for Associated Files](https://pdfa.org/resource/pdf-2-0-application-note-002-associated-files/)" is out of date as it does not account for PDF/A-4 nor [important errata for the use of Associated Files with marked content](https://pdf-issues.pdfa.org/32000-2-2020/clause14.html#H14.13.5). Terminology should also be clarified with the final edition of ISO 32000-2:2020, since this Application Note predates ISO publication.

In addition, updated use cases for LaTeX, EA-PDF and C2PA should be described.

issue.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - minor issues
issue.body:
Although I've mentioned them by email before, wanted to log them in an issue so we don't lose them.

1. There's a lot of time spent on the value of `NonFullScreenPageMode` on p62 of the spec, but by definition (in ISO32000) that value is only used if `PageMode` is `FullScreen`, which the EA-PDF spec says it's not allowed to be. So this could (and should) all be removed.
2. On page 67 we have the sentence "There SHALL only be at least one such entry in this AF array", which... should be improved. I believe from the context it's intended to mean "There SHALL be exactly one", but it could be "There SHALL be at least one". 
3. Typo in Tables 16 and 19, "case-sensistive"
4. I would like to note that using `ContentType` and `Checksum` in the Email _asset_ XMP type (Table 16), but `Content-Type` and `CheckSum` in the Email _attachment_ XMP type (Table 19) is horrible.

issue.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - minor issue (with collections)
issue.body:
Couple of minor points relating to EA-PDF collections.

1. The Collection Schema in Table 5 says that "Size" must be the size of the original email in bytes, but the example on the next page and in Table 6 say it has to have a Collection Schema Type of "Size" - if you check ISO32000:2 table 155, you'll see this type is _always_ evaluated as the size of the embedded file - the PDF containing the email - so it's not the size of the original email. If it's the size of the original email we want, it has to be set on the Embedded File params as an integer, and the schema type set to `N`.

2. I'd like to register a soft objection to "BCC" being a _required_ field in this schema, as for many workflows - ie. when you're dealing with received mail - this is going to be blank!

(edit)

3. Message-Id is listed as required in Table 6, but not in Table 5 - I'm not sure why we have two tables given the same information, but so long as we do they should match.

issue.title: EA-PDF - requirements when the PDF/A-4 file is tagged.
issue.body:
EA-PDF 1.0 has this on p74/75

> In all PDF/A-4 files with logical structure, the custom EA-PDF-defined semantics SHALL be included using a PDF 2.0 Namespace dictionary with an NS entry of `https://pdfa.org/ns/ea-pdf/mail-1` and including a `RoleMapNS` entry, as shown in Example 2 above. The following role map SHALL also be included (additional role mappings may also be included).
> |PDF 2.0 unique tags |Compatible PDF 1.7 tag
> |--|--
> |Private|Artifact
> |Aside|Div
> ... etc
>
> Reason: this RoleMap will be ignored by all PDF 2.0 processors for structure elements with an explicit namespace (NS entry), such as those defined by EA-PDF. However, PDF 1.7 only processors reading a PDF 2.0 EA-PDF file containing this RoleMap will use it to create a standard backward-compatible mapping to PDF 1.7 tags (since PDF 1.7 only processors do not support PDF 2.0 namespaces) providing a more consistent behaviour across processors.

There are several issues with this.

1. As described this doesn't make any sense: the table is supposed to be stored as a `RoleMapNS` entry, which is a PDF 2.0 field that is never going to be read by a PDF 1.0 processor. I think the first paragraph is supposed to use `RoleMap` where it used `RoleMapNS`
2. Why does this table have a fixed list of tags? If the "Private" tag is never used in the input PDF, why do we need to declare a rolemapping for it?

More generally, if the EA-Mail file is PDF 2.0 then it needs to be processed with a PDF 2.0 processor. Trying to "bodge" a compatibility layer into the file to try and convince a PDF 1.x processor that it is is safe to proceed in processing the tags is unwise in general. What if the PDF 2.0 tags are themselves rolemapped using RoleMapNS? What if the PDF 2.0 tags include MathML? The structure that results from the use of namespaces **can not** be represented without namespaces with 100% accuracy, so formally blessing an attempt to do so in a specification is not a good idea.

I think the RoleMap requirement really should be removed. If PDF 1.7 compatibility is a requirement, create a PDF 1.7 file.


-----
When creating a tagged PDF/A-4 document there is also this requirement:

> When PDF 2.0 (PDF/A-4) is used, PDF/mail-1 files with logical structure SHALL also conform to ISO TS 32005 and SHALL include the PDF Declaration for ISO TS 32005 in the document level XMP metadata (see https://pdfa.org/declarations/#ISO_TS_32005).
Reason: ISO TS 32005 standardizes the set of inclusion rules for the PDF 1.7 tag set, ensuring improved consistent behavior for reuse and accessibility across processors.

This looks fine on the surface, but I don't think it's a good idea to make this a SHALL requirement.

Assume you are starting with an HTML email, then the conversion to EA-PDF can either a) generate a tagged PDF, mapping the HTML tags to PDF tags, or b) create a non-tagged PDF.

It should be very obvious that preserving the tags, if possible, is the best option: they are part of the incoming email and have archival value (knowing content was marked as a header, a table or a code block is useful), and that value remains even if the tags are less than 100% perfect HTML.

But if the HTML tags are malformed, there is no guarantee that any conversion of those malformed tags to PDF tags would be well formed either. The tool converting this HTML to EA-PDF has to choose one of these options:
* Somehow post-process any invalid tags into a structure to make them valid according to ISO32005
* Write out the tags as they are, even if they're not ISO32005 compliant
* Discard the tags completely and don't create a tagged PDF

In practice, enforcing this requirement will push generators away from creating tagged EA-PDF files. It's going to achieve the exact opposite of what it's trying to do.

If it were me, I would make this a SHOULD requirement if tags from the input file are being preserved - something like:

> While EA-PDF creation tools should create PDFs that are also compliant with ISO TS 32005, this may not be possible if the tag structure in the incoming email is being preserved in the output PDF. If that is not the case then the logical structure SHALL conform to ISO TS 32005... *etc*

EDIT: it might be more clear if I point out that this requirement arguably contradicts this requirement on p74
> EA-PDF Creation Software SHOULD create equivalent PDF logical structure to that already present in
original source email content (such as encoded in HTML email bodies).

issue.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - more minor issues
issue.body:
* Section 9.5, requires that PDF/Mail-1c files that are PDF 1.7 shall specify ADBE extension level 5 - it should be **at least** 5.
* After talking to the Thinkbox team it's clear there are two ways to interpret the `xmp:CreateDate` which would be added to the XMP metadata - is it the date the email was created, or the date the PDF was created? I think they've convinced me it should be when the PDF was created, but a little guidance in the spec wouldn't hurt. For reference it's defined in ISO16684 as "_The date and time the resource was created. For a digital file, this need not match a file-system creation time. For a freshly created resource, it should be close to that time, modulo the time taken to write the file...._".
issue.display_title: EA-PDF 1.0 - more minor issues

issue.title: EA-PDF 1.0 - more minor issues
issue.display_title: EA-PDF 1.0 - more minor issues

comments.body:
* Until/unless Adobe publicly releases their documentation for ADBE extension levels greater than 5, EA-PDF needs to stick with **exactly** 5. ADBE extension 5 documentation has been freely publicly available for many years. The later ADBE Extension levels were originally restricted under their NDA / pre-release licensing and were not publicly available to my knowledge. Even though these documents are now many years old, the legal situation still remains.

* Re XMP `xmp:CreateDate` - I think this should follow existing PDF/A "best practices"... which is (AFAICT) highly variable and depends on vendor SW. I have PDF/A examples with both - the date of the original asset AND the date of the conversion of the original asset into PDF/A.  AFAICT there is no firm guidance in any PDF/A standard or any PDF Association TechNote that clarifies this, so it is probably worthwhile asking in PDF/A TWG or WG 5 to see if there is a "preferred" understanding by the archival community before anything is mandated by EA-PDF. There are also several other date fields in "well known" XMP Part 2 under **stEvt**, **stRef** as well as the PDF/A Provenance **xmpMM** which could also be used.

I'd be very dismayed with an app that failed to use the PDF's creation date as the CreateDate in XMP. 

If someone wants to attach the source that's up to them and a fine thing to do, but the PDF is the PDF, not an ersatz source file...
Its nothing to do with "_PDF's creation date as the CreateDate in XMP_, but other kinds of inputs.

Maybe I misunderstood something, but my comment was based on:

> After talking to the Thinkbox team it's clear there are two ways to interpret the xmp:CreateDate which would be added to the XMP metadata - is it the date the email was created, or the date the PDF was created? I think they've convinced me it should be when the PDF was created

I was agreeing with @faceless2. 

If "general practice" varies on this, as you imply, then EA-PDF should, IMHO, cover this point normatively (whatever general PDF creation software does, EA-PDFs aren't a "general" case).

issue.title: Accessibility issues with the Hierarchical inclusion rules excel document
issue.body:
The Excel [Hierarchical inclusion rules – PDF Association](https://pdfa.org/resource/iso-ts-32005-hierarchical-inclusion-rules/) does not meet Microsoft's Excel recommendations [Make your content accessible in the Microsoft 365 apps | Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/accessibility/office-accessibility/make-your-content-accessible-in-the-microsoft-365-apps).

1. The table includes two levels of column headings, two levels of row headings (which is not accessible in Microsoft Office products)
2. The table is not formatted as a table
3. The table is not named
4. The table title is not formatted as a heading
5. The only defined name is the print area.

issue.title: Accessibility of Alt and Contents for Link Annotations, with Brotli document
issue.body:
OK, are you saying here that the link is about 'Clause 8.9.7' say, and no-one gets more information about it until they visit the site?
If the intention is for the link to be taking you into the external ISO document itself, then this I would agree with.

But the links here are taking you to a Bibliographic entry, or Normative Reference entry, on another page within the same PDF. This is not stated anywhere in the immediate context of where the link occurs. The purpose of the link seems to me to be to get you to a place where you can find a way to visit the external document. Without the Alt text this is not clear at all, until having followed the link and discovered this for yourself. So having Bib... (or Norm...) in the Alt/popup text is complying with the Level A interpretation, surely?

On the other hand if you were to change all the links to go directly to the external ISO (or PDFA-sponsored) PDF, each targeting the specific page where the clause or table appears, then the Alt text should also be changed. (If there's a pay-wall along the way, then this ought to be mentioned.)
